title: Russian missile, drone assault leaves at least 12 dead across Ukraine
summary: Russian missiles and drones pounded Kyiv and a dozen other Ukrainian regions overnight into Wednesday, killing at least 12 civilians, including three children, and wounding more than 40 in Moscow's…

image.caption: Emergency services work to rescue residents from under the debris at the site of an apartment building hit by a Russian missile strike in the town of Pryluky, amid Russia’s attack on Ukraine, on Wednesday. (Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Russian missiles and drones pounded Kyiv and a dozen other Ukrainian regions overnight into Wednesday, killing at least 12 civilians, including three children, and wounding more than 40 in Moscow's latest devastating barrage, Ukrainian officials said.
Most of the dead were killed in a strike on apartment block in Pryluky in northern Ukraine

Ukraine had anticipated the attack, with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warning the previous day that intelligence services had concluded that Russia was building up for a "massive" strike. He said Russia had fired 70 missiles and drones.
Although Ukraine knew about the looming attack, which coincided with Russian President Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday, it couldn't fend it off completely.

A Russian strike destroyed an apartment block in Pryluky, in Ukraine's northern Chernihiv region, killing nine people, including three children, and wounding 34, Interior Minister Ihor Vyhivskyi said.

In this photo provided by the Ukrainian Emergency Service, rescuers work on the scene of a building destroyed following recent Russian attacks in Pryluky on Wednesday. (Ukrainian Emergency Service/The Associated Press)
Deaths were also reported in three other Ukrainian cities, including Kyiv, according to Zelenskyy.
"The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively," the Ukrainian leader said on social media.

blocks.text: Ukraine is looking worldwide for available Patriot missiles, which are in short supply due to the Iran war.
"Russian ballistic missiles remain the greatest challenge. And air defence packages for us right now are a vital necessity," Zelenskyy said.
Russia says it targeted missile storage, production sites
In Kremenchuk, in the Poltava region, two people were killed and seven injured, said Vitalii Diakivnych, head of the regional military administration. A rescue operation was continuing.

"That is exactly what the enemy is counting on. For us to be afraid to fall asleep. To let our children out of our sight. To plan anything. So that everyone thinks: next time it could be my address," he said.
The children abducted by Putin’s war machine

Russia's Defence Ministry said the military carried out a massive strike overnight targeting industrial facilities involved in the production and storage of missiles and drones across Ukraine. Targets ‌included sites where the company Fire Point makes and stores Flamingo ⁠cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv, ‌as well as in the regions of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava and ​Kharkiv, it said.

The ministry said that port and ship repair facilities in the southern Odesa region and ships carrying cargo for the Ukrainian military were also hit.
Ukraine has hit back at Russia by launching long-range drones and missiles on oil refineries and storage depots.
Zelenskyy said Wednesday that Ukraine targeted two oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions of Russia.
Russian officials made no immediate comment.

blocks.text: Zelenskyy also indicated that Ukraine had struck in the Black Sea. He posted images of a fire said to show an oil tanker burning in the water near the Russian city of Sochi.
It was not possible to independently verify the images.

The deaths and damage illustrated the difficulty Ukraine has in countering Russia's ballistic missiles and the new jet-powered drones used in Moscow's escalating bombardments. Without ammunition for its U.S.-made Patriot air defence systems, Ukraine can't stop Russian ballistic weapons. It is racing to develop a new generation of interceptors fast enough to catch Moscow's high-flying jet-propelled drones.
Escalating Russian attacks on Ukrainian ports is making shipping risky

Russia and Ukraine are engaged in a long-range aerial war as their armies remain largely deadlocked on the battlefield, more than 4½ years after Moscow's all-out invasion of its neighbour. The unrelenting aerial attacks are hurting Russia but could be ruinous for smaller Ukraine.
Putin is pressing ahead with the invasion in the belief that Ukrainians will buckle under the pressure and Kyiv's Western supporters won't stay the course, Western analysts say.
